rounds.text: GPT Healthcare Ltd represents a highly compelling opportunity as it trades at a significant discount to its peers, with a P/E of 22.33x against a sector benchmark of 35.47x [E6] and an EV/EBITDA of 11.43x against the sector's 20.84x [E11], while simultaneously delivering superior capital efficiency, including an ROE of 28.53% compared to the sector benchmark of 15.71% [E9]. This operational strength is backed by exceptional cash generation, with a cash conversion rate of 1.93x [E28] and operating cash flow representing 110% of operating profit in March 2026 [E31], which is set to be further leveraged as capital expenditure is largely completed with capital work-in-progress down 97.8% [E34]. The market has underappreciated this setup, as a reverse discounted cash flow analysis shows the current price implies only 14.7% earnings growth [E41], which is well below the company's trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 16% [E16] and its 5-year compounded profit growth of 16% [E17]. Conceded: [E19], [E24], and [E33] show a -13% decline in trailing twelve-month profit growth, a 3 percentage point contraction in operating margins over three years, and borrowings rising to Rs 91 Cr. However, the business remains highly robust, supported by a strong sector tailwind [E63], a rules-based screen score of 89 out of 100 [E55], and strong price momentum with a relative-strength rating of 92 against the Nifty 500 [E45].

GPT Healthcare trades at a high P/E of 31.3 [E1] and a price-to-book ratio of 5.00x [E2], which is difficult to justify given that its compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months has fallen to -13% [E19] and is only 4% over three years [E18]. This earnings deterioration is driven by contracting profitability, as the operating margin dropped to 18% in March 2026 from 21% three years prior [E24], while borrowings simultaneously escalated to Rs 91 Cr from Rs 35 Cr a year earlier [E33]. Institutional investors are actively retreating, with foreign institutional holding dropping by 3.65 percentage points [E36] and domestic institutional holding falling by 4.67 percentage points [E37] since March 2024, alongside a -34.4% decrease in promoter holdings over the last three years [E54]. Conceded: [E12], [E28], and [E63] show that the company maintains a healthy return on capital employed, strong cash conversion, and operates within a sector experiencing a macro tailwind.

Conceded: [E1] and [E2]. While headline valuation multiples appear elevated on a standalone basis, they completely ignore the company's significant discount to sector benchmarks across P/E of 22.33x versus 35.47x, P/B of 3.5x versus 4.87x, and EV/EBITDA of 11.43x versus 20.84x [E6, E7, E11]. Conceded: [E19] and [E18]. However, trailing metrics obscure fundamental business efficiency, evidenced by an elite ROA of 15.01%, ROE of 28.53%, and ROCE of 23.48% that heavily outperform sector medians [E8, E9, E10]. Conceded: [E24]. Nevertheless, margin compression is counterbalanced by exceptional cash generation where operating cash flow covers 110% of operating profit alongside a 1.93x cash conversion rate [E28, E31]. Conceded: [E33], [E36], and [E37]. Despite rising borrowings and institutional share shifts, the business has successfully deployed capital into completed capacity expansion with CWIP dropping 97.8% [E34], and recent institutional money flow has actually turned positive with a holding change of +0.32 percentage points [E38].

Conceded: [E6, E7, E11]. The bull relies on relative valuation discounts against sector benchmarks, yet a P/E of 31.3x and a price-to-book of 5.00x reflect an expensive absolute price [E1, E2] backed by a mere 9.1% margin of safety [E40]. Conceded: [E8, E9, E10]. Superior return metrics cannot whitewash a severe contraction in profitability, evidenced by compounded profit growth plummeting to -13% over the trailing twelve months and slowing to 4% over three years [E18, E19]. Conceded: [E28, E31]. While cash conversion looks strong, operating margins have degraded by 3 percentage points over three years to 18% in Mar 2026, exhibiting an inconsistent trend [E24, E26]. Conceded: [E34]. The completion of capital expenditure has coincided with borrowings surging from Rs 35 Cr to Rs 91 Cr in Mar 2026 [E33]. Conceded: [E38]. Despite a fractional one-quarter uptick in institutional holdings, foreign and domestic institutions have dumped their stakes significantly over the longer term—dropping by 3.65 and 4.67 percentage points respectively since Mar 2024 [E36, E37]—while promoter holdings have decreased by 34.4% over the last 3 years [E54].
